beats.say: The solution to a system of equations is the point where their graphs cross. Desmos finds that point for you with a single click.
You do not need to rearrange equations into y equals form. Desmos graphs equations written in almost any form.
We will work through three examples, from easy to hard, and each one ends by reading the crossing point.
Easy example. Solve the system y equals x plus one, and y equals two x minus two.
Open Desmos on a fresh graph. Each equation of the system will go in its own row.
Type the first equation, y equals x plus one. Desmos draws the line immediately.
Now type the second equation, y equals two x minus two. A second line appears, with a different slope.
The solution is where the two lines cross. Click the crossing point, and then click its grey dot, to see the coordinates three comma four.
So x equals three and y equals four. We can check by putting three into both equations, and each one gives four.
Medium example. This time the equations are not in y equals form. Solve three x plus two y equals twelve, and x minus y equals negative one.
On the SAT, systems usually come in standard form. In Desmos, that is not a problem, because we can type them exactly as they are written.
Type three x plus two y equals twelve. Desmos graphs the line without any rearranging.
Now type x minus y equals negative one. Again, Desmos draws the second line directly.
Click where the lines cross, and then click the grey dot. Desmos shows the point two comma three.
So x equals two and y equals three. Check: three times two plus two times three is twelve, and two minus three is negative one.
Hard example. For the system four x plus y equals nineteen, and x minus two y equals negative two, what is the value of three x minus y?
Notice that the question does not ask for x or y. It asks for three x minus y. So we first find the solution, and then compute.
Type the first equation, four x plus y equals nineteen. It is a steep line sloping downward.
Type the second equation, x minus two y equals negative two. It is a gentler line sloping upward.
Click the crossing point, and then its grey dot. Desmos shows the point four comma three, so x is four and y is three.
Now compute what the question asked. Three times four is twelve, and twelve minus three is nine. So the answer is nine, with no symbolic solving.
To recap. The solution of a system is the point where the graphs cross, so graph both equations and click that point.
Parallel lines never cross, so a system with parallel lines has no solution. The same line twice means infinitely many solutions.
If the question asks for an expression like three x minus y, find x and y first, then compute. In the next video, we solve any equation by graphing.
